items.b: PUDONG DEVELOPMENT BANK ENDS RETAIL SHANGHAI GOLD EXCHANGE TRADING AFTER 25 SEPTEMBER
items.t: Shanghai Pudong Development Bank will discontinue its agency service for Shanghai Gold Exchange personal precious-metals business at a time of its choosing after 25 September 2026, closing mobile banking, online banking and branch counter channels. The suspension covers 9 contract codes, from Au99.99 to Ag(T+D). ICBC and China Construction Bank closed the same business on 24 July 2026, and Postal Savings Bank, Ping An Bank and Guangfa Bank filed earlier suspensions in the first half of the year, making 6 banks out of the channel in 2026. Bank staff told the 21st Century Business Herald that the exchange had decided to shut individual-client trading altogether, citing market instability and policy requirements; that account is attributed to those staff, not to the exchange, and no statement on the exchange's own site was located.

items.b: SIGNET COMPS RISE 2.2% AS TOTAL SALES FALL 0.5% AND 53 STORES COME OUT
items.t: Signet Jewelers reported same store sales up 2.2% for the 13 weeks ended 1 August 2026, with total sales down 0.5% to $1,528.1 million from $1,535.1 million. The chain closed 53 stores and opened 5 since year-end Fiscal 2026, leaving 2,534 open and selling space down 1.1% to 4.0 million square feet; North America took 50 of the closures. Operating income was $87.5 million against $2.8 million, and adjusted diluted EPS $2.19 against $1.61. Gross margin of 39.4% was helped by about $15 million of refunds for tariffs previously paid, with higher gold costs named as an offset. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance rises to $10.45 to $12.15 from $9.20 to $11.00, a midpoint 11.9% higher, while the full-year sales range is unchanged at $6.7 to $6.9 billion.

items.b: SOTHEBY'S OFFERS HKD 2M COLORED-DIAMOND EARRINGS WITHOUT RESERVE IN HONG KONG
items.t: A pair of colored-diamond earrings pairing a 2.08-carat light pink pear shape with a 2.21-carat very light pink VVS1 carries a HKD 2 million high estimate, or $255,050, at Sotheby's Fine Jewelry sale in Hong Kong on 9 September, offered without reserve. More than 300 pieces are in the sale, including Graff, Tiffany and Hermès. Three of the five largest named lots carry no reserve: the earrings, a ruby and diamond demi-parure with 60 Burmese rubies of 26.78 carats at HKD 600,000 to 1,200,000, and a 3.10-carat Mozambique ruby ring at HKD 500,000 to 1,000,000. A 0.88-carat fancy vivid purplish pink ring is estimated at HKD 800,000 to 1,500,000.

items.b: PALLADIUM SHEDS $36.00 TO $1,335.00 AGAINST THE 8 SEPTEMBER MARK
items.t: On Kitco's bid at 10:04 UTC, palladium fell $36.00 to $1,335.00, a fall of 2.6258% and the only move of the four metals past one percent. Gold eased to $4,389.30, platinum rose to $1,841.00 and silver to $66.13. Palladium's bid-ask spread widened to 2.9963% of the bid from 2.9176%, and the metal covered $66.00 on the session. The gold-silver ratio narrowed to 66.4 ounces from 66.7. Changes are measured against the 8 September marks in this paper's own record; Kitco's own change field runs from its prior close and prints all four metals higher. No source read named a cause.

items.b: HERITAGE PUTS A $250,000 HIGH ESTIMATE ON A 22.09-CARAT FANCY YELLOW
items.t: Heritage Auctions estimated a 22.09-carat fancy yellow diamond, Internally Flawless and documented to South Africa's Kimberley mine, at $200,000 to $250,000 for its Fall Fine Jewelry Signature Auction on 28 September. The house names the stone the Kimberley Sunshine and Pragnell as the maker of the piece. The range works out at $9,054 to $11,317 a carat on 22.09 carats, before buyer's premium, and the high sits $50,000 above the low, a spread of 25.0% of the low estimate.
